_comment: Canonical settings.json wiring for this repo, merged into ~/.claude/settings.json
by devcontainer-config/link-claude-home.sh at container start (decision 023).
Two sections, both merged as (existing - ours) + ours:
hooks       — event key -> matcher groups
permissions — mode (deny/ask/allow) -> rule strings
{{CLAUDE_DIR}} is substituted with the resolved config dir (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or
$HOME/.claude) at merge time — do not hardcode $HOME here: the token has to survive
a config dir that is not ~/.claude.
Merging is by exact match on each entry, so re-running the linker is idempotent and
never touches entries this file did not put there. That also means any edit to an
entry below strands the previous version in an already-merged settings.json: bump it
in the same commit as a linker run, or prune by hand.
Every hook here is non-blocking EXCEPT guard-trusted-writes.py (denies writes to
trusted-policy paths) and auto-approve-allowed-commands.sh (grants permission).
Those two sit on the permission path — see decision 023 for why they are on by
default and how to opt out (CC_SKIP_HOOK_WIRING=1).
The permissions.deny block is not decoration: guard-trusted-writes.py DEFERS on its
HARD tier for the file tools rather than returning 'ask', because a hook 'ask' would
silently override permissions.deny (Claude Code issue #39344). The deny rules below
are what actually does the blocking on that path. Wiring the hook without them left
the HARD tier a no-op for Edit/Write — decision 023 amendment B.
